sections.title: Stage 3 · Apprentice: big friends
sections.html:
Stage 3 · Apprentice: big friends

Nine lessons on carrying and borrowing. Big friends make 10, and they are the moment the abacus gets faster than fingers and paper.

Where this stage goes

The level goal. Carry and borrow between columns with the eighteen big-friend (10) formulas, in 5-line problems.

In plain words. Carry and borrow between columns with the "make 10" trick. Five-line sums on the beads. The abacus is now faster than fingers and paper.

How long. 5–6 weeks at fifteen minutes a day, six days a week.

A rod holds 9 at most. When a sum goes past 9, one bead moves to the rod on the left, and the rod gives back the difference from 10. When a take-away needs more than the rod has, one bead comes back from the left.

Two numbers that make 10 are big friends: 1 and 9, 2 and 8, 3 and 7, 4 and 6, 5 and 5. To add a number that will not fit, take away its big friend and carry 1. To take away a number that is not there, add its big friend, then borrow 1.

Order matters on a real abacus. Work the rod you are on first, then the rod to its left. For adding: take away the friend, then carry. For taking away: add the friend, then borrow. One rule for both.

The drills in this stage

  • Two rods. A start number up to 99 and one digit. Watch the tens rod change on every carry and borrow.
  • Written. Five-line columns of 2-digit numbers, adds first, then plus and minus mixed.
  • Dictation. Read a 5-line column out loud while your child works it on the beads.
  • Mental. Three, then four one-digit numbers in the head, now crossing ten.

Accuracy before speed

Carries feel backwards for about a week. That is normal. Hold the pass marks at 9 of 10 on the two-rod pages and do not add a clock anywhere in this stage. A child who carries correctly and slowly will be fast by Stage 5. A child who carries quickly and wrong has to unlearn it.

Where this sits on the abacus ladders

Five-line columns of 2-digit numbers are the format of 10th kyu, the first graded level of the Japanese abacus exams. In UCMAS terms this is still Foundation, the last part of it. The mental lesson at the end of the stage is Bead Score rung 2 and 3 work: any two digits, then a running total, crossing ten.

The 18 moves of this stage

In this book these moves are blue. Adds first, then take-aways.

sections.title: Lesson 3.1 · +9, +8, +7
sections.html:
Lesson 3.1 · +9, +8, +7

Lesson 17 of 76. Stage 3, lesson 1 of 9. About 15 minutes. You need your abacus and a grown-up beside you.

By the end, your child can add 9, 8 or 7 to a rod when it will not fit, by taking away the big friend and carrying 1.

The move

Set 4. Add 9. There is no room: 4 and 9 is more than one rod can hold.

So use the big friend of 9, which is 1. Take 1 away from this rod. Then carry 1 to the tens rod. The rod shows 3 and the tens rod shows 1. That is 13.

Plus 8 takes away 2 and carries. Plus 7 takes away 3 and carries. Say it every time: "plus 8, take away 2, carry 1."

Worked example. Start at 4. Add 9, then 8.

  • Start with .
  • + 9. Ones rod, plus 9: take away 1, carry 1 to the left. Tens rod, the carry (plus 1): the beads are free. Now .
  • + 8. Ones rod, plus 8: take away 2, carry 1 to the left. Tens rod, the carry (plus 1): the beads are free. Now .
  • Read it: 21.
Parent lineAsk your child to say the order out loud, friend off first and then the carry, until the hand does it without the words.

Drill

Set the first number on two rods. Then add the digit. Watch the tens rod. Write what the beads show. Pass mark: 9 of 10 right. Not yet? Same page tomorrow.

12345
67 + 817 + 94 + 727 + 948 + 8
678910
12 + 843 + 854 + 93 + 961 + 9

Stuck? Small friends make 5: 1 and 4, 2 and 3. Cannot add 3? Add 5 and take away 2. Big friends make 10: 1 and 9, 2 and 8, 3 and 7, 4 and 6, 5 and 5. Cannot add 8? Take away 2 and carry 1 to the left.

Next: Lesson 3.2 · +6 and +5.

sections.title: Lesson 3.2 · +6 and +5
sections.html:
Lesson 3.2 · +6 and +5

Lesson 18 of 76. Stage 3, lesson 2 of 9. About 12 minutes. You need your abacus and a grown-up beside you.

By the end, your child can add 6 or 5 to a rod that is too full, with the big friend and a carry.

The move

Plus 6 takes away 4 and carries 1. Plus 5 takes away 5 and carries 1.

Plus 5 with a carry only happens when the top bead is already down. You need another 5 and there is no second top bead. So the top bead goes up, and 1 goes to the left.

If the rod does not have the friend to take away, the move is a combination. That comes in Stage 4, and this drill never asks for one.

Worked example. Start at 9. Add 6, then 5.

  • Start with .
  • + 6. Ones rod, plus 6: take away 4, carry 1 to the left. Tens rod, the carry (plus 1): the beads are free. Now .
  • + 5. Ones rod, plus 5: take away 5, carry 1 to the left. Tens rod, the carry (plus 1): the beads are free. Now .
  • Read it: 20.
Parent lineAsk "does it fit?" before every move, because that one question picks the right friend.

Drill

Set the first number on two rods. Then add the digit. Watch the tens rod. Write what the beads show. Pass mark: 9 of 10 right. Not yet? Same page tomorrow.

12345
4 + 69 + 664 + 658 + 534 + 6
678910
67 + 545 + 569 + 527 + 536 + 5

Stuck? Small friends make 5: 1 and 4, 2 and 3. Cannot add 3? Add 5 and take away 2. Big friends make 10: 1 and 9, 2 and 8, 3 and 7, 4 and 6, 5 and 5. Cannot add 8? Take away 2 and carry 1 to the left.

Next: Lesson 3.3 · +4, +3, +2, +1 past nine.

sections.title: Lesson 3.3 · +4, +3, +2, +1 past nine
sections.html:
Lesson 3.3 · +4, +3, +2, +1 past nine

Lesson 19 of 76. Stage 3, lesson 3 of 9. About 12 minutes. You need your abacus and a grown-up beside you.

By the end, your child can carry when a small number lands on a nearly full rod.

The move

Small numbers can overflow too. 9 + 1 does not fit on one rod. Take away 9, carry 1.

Every digit has a big friend, so every digit has a carry move. Plus 4 takes away 6. Plus 3 takes away 7. Plus 2 takes away 8. Plus 1 takes away 9.

Here a small friend can hide inside the big one. Take away 6 from a rod showing 7: that is the top bead and one bottom bead, straight off. Free. Then carry.

Worked example. Start at 7. Add 4.

  • Start with .
  • + 4. Ones rod, plus 4: take away 6, carry 1 to the left. Tens rod, the carry (plus 1): the beads are free. Now .
  • Read it: 11.
Parent lineIf your child freezes on a small number, ask "does it fit?" and point at the rod, not the bead.

Drill

Set the first number on two rods. Then add the digit. Watch the tens rod. Write what the beads show. Pass mark: 9 of 10 right. Not yet? Same page tomorrow.

12345
9 + 359 + 168 + 328 + 268 + 4
678910
27 + 428 + 426 + 489 + 367 + 4

Stuck? Small friends make 5: 1 and 4, 2 and 3. Cannot add 3? Add 5 and take away 2. Big friends make 10: 1 and 9, 2 and 8, 3 and 7, 4 and 6, 5 and 5. Cannot add 8? Take away 2 and carry 1 to the left.

Next: Lesson 3.4 · Carry chains.

sections.title: Lesson 3.4 · Carry chains
sections.html:
Lesson 3.4 · Carry chains

Lesson 20 of 76. Stage 3, lesson 4 of 9. About 15 minutes. You need your abacus and a grown-up beside you.

By the end, your child can carry across two or three rods in a row, in 5-line columns of 2-digit adds.

The move

Sometimes the carry itself does not fit. 99 + 1: the ones rod takes away 9 and carries. The tens rod already shows 9, so it takes away 9 and carries again. The hundreds rod gets 1. That is 100.

Each carry is just another plus 1, with the same rules. Your child already knows them.

Now real sums: five lines of two digits, adding only, with small and big friends mixed. Use the abacus.

Worked example. Start at 97. Add 4, then 99.

  • Start with .
  • + 4. Ones rod, plus 4: take away 6, carry 1 to the left. Tens rod, the carry (plus 1): take away 9, carry 1 to the left. Hundreds rod, the carry (plus 1): the beads are free. Now .
  • + 99. Tens rod, plus 9: the beads are free. Ones rod, plus 9: take away 1, carry 1 to the left. Tens rod, the carry (plus 1): take away 9, carry 1 to the left. Hundreds rod, the carry (plus 1): the beads are free. Now .
  • Read it: 200.
Parent lineLet the carry chains be slow and correct, because speed here comes on its own by Stage 5.

Drill

Stuck? Small friends make 5: 1 and 4, 2 and 3. Cannot add 3? Add 5 and take away 2. Big friends make 10: 1 and 9, 2 and 8, 3 and 7, 4 and 6, 5 and 5. Cannot add 8? Take away 2 and carry 1 to the left.

sections.title: Lesson 3.5 · −9, −8, −7: borrowing
sections.html:
Lesson 3.5 · −9, −8, −7: borrowing

Lesson 21 of 76. Stage 3, lesson 5 of 9. About 15 minutes. You need your abacus and a grown-up beside you.

By the end, your child can take away 9, 8 or 7 when the rod does not have enough, by adding the big friend and borrowing 1.

The move

Set 13. Take away 9. The ones rod shows 3. There is no 9 to take.

So add the big friend of 9, which is 1. The ones rod shows 4. Then borrow: take 1 from the tens rod. That is minus 10. Add 1 and take away 10, and you have taken away 9. That is 13 − 9 = 4.

Minus 8 adds 2, then borrows. Minus 7 adds 3, then borrows. Say it as you move: "Minus 9: add 1, borrow 1 from the left."

Worked example. Start at 31. Take away 9, then 8.

  • Start with .
  • − 9. Ones rod, minus 9: add 1, borrow 1 from the left. Tens rod, the borrow (minus 1): the beads are there. Now .
  • − 8. Ones rod, minus 8: add 2, borrow 1 from the left. Tens rod, the borrow (minus 1): the beads are there. Now .
  • Read it: 14.
Parent lineSay "add the friend, then borrow" once at the start of the page and then keep your hands in your lap.

Drill

Set the first number on two rods. Then take away the digit. Watch the tens rod. Write what the beads show. Pass mark: 9 of 10 right. Not yet? Same page tomorrow.

12345
10 − 970 − 731 − 970 − 925 − 8
678910
25 − 987 − 976 − 940 − 750 − 7

Stuck? Small friends make 5: 1 and 4, 2 and 3. Cannot add 3? Add 5 and take away 2. Big friends make 10: 1 and 9, 2 and 8, 3 and 7, 4 and 6, 5 and 5. Cannot add 8? Take away 2 and carry 1 to the left.

Next: Lesson 3.6 · −6 down to −1.

sections.title: Lesson 3.6 · −6 down to −1
sections.html:
Lesson 3.6 · −6 down to −1

Lesson 22 of 76. Stage 3, lesson 6 of 9. About 15 minutes. You need your abacus and a grown-up beside you.

By the end, your child can borrow for any digit from 6 down to 1.

The move

Same move for every digit. Add the big friend here, then borrow 1 from the left.

Minus 6 adds 4. Minus 5 adds 5. Minus 4 adds 6. Minus 3 adds 7. Minus 2 adds 8. Minus 1 adds 9.

A child who knows the five pairs that make 10 knows all of these. If a move stalls, ask for the friend first, then the move.

Worked example. Start at 20. Take away 6, then 5.

  • Start with .
  • − 6. Ones rod, minus 6: add 4, borrow 1 from the left. Tens rod, the borrow (minus 1): the beads are there. Now .
  • − 5. Ones rod, minus 5: add 5, borrow 1 from the left. Tens rod, the borrow (minus 1): the beads are there. Now .
  • Read it: 9.
Parent lineAsk "who is the friend of 6?" before you ask anything else.

Drill

Set the first number on two rods. Then take away the digit. Watch the tens rod. Write what the beads show. Pass mark: 9 of 10 right. Not yet? Same page tomorrow.

12345
90 − 610 − 312 − 455 − 670 − 4
678910
13 − 462 − 580 − 252 − 381 − 3

Stuck? Small friends make 5: 1 and 4, 2 and 3. Cannot add 3? Add 5 and take away 2. Big friends make 10: 1 and 9, 2 and 8, 3 and 7, 4 and 6, 5 and 5. Cannot add 8? Take away 2 and carry 1 to the left.

Next: Lesson 3.7 · Borrow chains and mixed problems.

sections.title: Lesson 3.7 · Borrow chains and mixed problems
sections.html:
Lesson 3.7 · Borrow chains and mixed problems

Lesson 23 of 76. Stage 3, lesson 7 of 9. About 15 minutes. You need your abacus and a grown-up beside you.

By the end, your child can borrow across empty rods and work 5-line columns with plus and minus mixed.

The move

100 − 1: the ones rod is empty, so add 9, then borrow 1 from the tens. The tens rod is empty too, so it does the same: add 9, then borrow 1 from the hundreds. 100 − 1 = 99.

A borrow chain is a carry chain run backwards. Each borrow is a minus 1 on the next rod, with the same rules.

Now plus and minus mixed, five lines. Every move from the first three stages is in play. This is the real thing.

Worked example. Start at 100. Take away 1, then add 45.

  • Start with .
  • − 1. Ones rod, minus 1: add 9, borrow 1 from the left. Tens rod, the borrow (minus 1): add 9, borrow 1 from the left. Hundreds rod, the borrow (minus 1): the beads are there. Now .
  • + 45. Tens rod, plus 4: take away 6, carry 1 to the left. Hundreds rod, the carry (plus 1): the beads are free. Ones rod, plus 5: take away 5, carry 1 to the left. Tens rod, the carry (plus 1): the beads are free. Now .
  • Read it: 144.
Parent lineThis is the page where accuracy slips, so praise every correct borrow you hear said out loud.

sections.title: Lesson 3.8 · Mental: small friends in the head
sections.html:
Lesson 3.8 · Mental: small friends in the head

Lesson 24 of 76. Stage 3, lesson 8 of 9. About 8 minutes. You need no abacus. A pencil for the answers only.

By the end, your child can add and take away three one-digit numbers in the head when a small friend is needed.

The move

Abacus away. Three numbers, one digit each, and every sum needs a small friend somewhere.

See the top bead come down in your mind. See the friend beads go. Move the fingers on the table if it helps. Most children do at this point, and the habit fades on its own later.

Worked example. Picture an empty rod. Add 4, add 3, take away 2.

  • Start with .
  • + 4. Ones rod, plus 4: the beads are free. Now .
  • + 3. Ones rod, plus 3: add 5, take away 2. Now .
  • − 2. Ones rod, minus 2: the beads are there. Now .
  • Read it: 5.
Parent lineCover the abacus with a tea towel so it is out of sight, and wait out the silence.

Drill

No abacus. Read the column, move the beads in your head, write only the answer. Pass mark: 9 of 10 right. Not yet? Same page tomorrow.

12345
69275
−4−6+4−4−4
−2+2+2+6+7
678910
68621
−2−7−4+4+4
−2+4+6+1−1

Stuck? Small friends make 5: 1 and 4, 2 and 3. Cannot add 3? Add 5 and take away 2. If the picture collapses into words, do the same sum once on the real abacus, close your eyes, and replay it.

sections.title: Lesson 3.9 · Mental: crossing ten
sections.html:
Lesson 3.9 · Mental: crossing ten

Lesson 25 of 76. Stage 3, lesson 9 of 9. About 8 minutes. You need no abacus. A pencil for the answers only.

By the end, your child can keep a running total in the head as it crosses ten, with four one-digit numbers.

The move

Now the total in the picture passes 10. Picture two rods. When the ones rod overflows, a bead appears on the tens rod.

Four numbers, one digit each, plus and minus. Every sum on this page carries or borrows at least once.

If the picture falls apart, do the same sum once on the real abacus. Watch it. Close your eyes and replay it. Then try the next one in the head.

Worked example. Picture two empty rods. Add 8, add 7, take away 3, add 4.

  • Start with .
  • + 8. Ones rod, plus 8: the beads are free. Now .
  • + 7. Ones rod, plus 7: take away 3, carry 1 to the left. Tens rod, the carry (plus 1): the beads are free. Now .
  • − 3. Ones rod, minus 3: take away 5, add 2. Now .
  • + 4. Ones rod, plus 4: add 5, take away 1. Now .
  • Read it: 16.
Parent lineA wrong head sum costs nothing, so say "next one" and keep the beat going.

Drill

No abacus. Read the column, move the beads in your head, write only the answer. Pass mark: 8 of 10 right. Not yet? Same page tomorrow.

Take away 2 and carry 1 to the left. If the picture collapses into words, do the same sum once on the real abacus, close your eyes, and replay it.

sections.title: Stage 3 quest cards
sections.html:
Stage 3 quest cards

Three short cards. They repeat the stage in miniature: one move, one column, one sum in the head.

Quest Q6 · Carry or borrow

sections.title: The Apprentice Boss
sections.html:
The Apprentice Boss

Take the boss when every lesson is passed and a 5-line column feels calm. Part 1 maps to Lessons 3.1 to 3.6. Part 2 maps to 3.4 and 3.7. Part 3 maps to 3.9.

The printed test is Boss 3 in boss-tests.md. It has 3 parts:

  • Carry or borrow. 10 moves on your abacus. Need 9 of 10 in 2 minutes 30 seconds.
  • 2-digit, 5 lines. 6 problems on your abacus. Need 5 of 6 in 5 minutes.
  • Mental. 5 problems, four 1-digit numbers each. Need 4 of 5 in 2 minutes 30 seconds.

sections.title: What the trainer adds to this stage
sections.html:
What the trainer adds to this stage

The trainer's two-rod drill draws the tens rod right beside the ones rod, so your child sees the carry land. That small picture does a lot of teaching in the first week of this stage.

It also mixes carries and borrows at random once both are learned, which is hard to do by hand without a problem book. And it shows the move after any miss, so a wrong carry gets fixed on the spot instead of at the end of the page.
